intro: Every video here is a screen recording of something running, not a slide deck. The rule from the pipeline holds: show the terminal before explaining it, because the proof earns the explanation. Grouped into series, because a series gets subscribed to and a loose video does not.

groups.title: Series: Proxies, one pattern at a time
groups.note: The strongest series you can ship. Each episode is one pattern, built live, broken live.

items.t: Delegatecall storage collision in five minutes
items.d: The shortest possible demonstration of why proxy storage layout matters. The hook for the whole series.

items.t: Minimal proxy (EIP-1167) assembly deep dive
items.d: Read the 45 bytes of runtime code opcode by opcode, then deploy a clone with it.

items.t: Transparent versus UUPS, built side by side
items.d: Two proxies, one admin-collision bug, demonstrated rather than described.

items.t: Beacon proxy: upgrading a hundred contracts at once
items.d: Deploy many, upgrade once, show every instance change behaviour in the same transaction.

items.t: Bricking a UUPS proxy live
items.d: Uninitialised implementation plus selfdestruct, and the recovery that does not exist.

items.t: Diamond proxy: adding and removing a facet on camera
items.d: DiamondCut in practice, with the loupe showing the facet set change.

groups.title: Series: Live exploits
groups.note: Each episode: the vulnerable contract, the exploit test going green, then the fix. Twelve to twenty minutes.

items.t: Reentrancy on a minimal staking contract
items.d: The canonical bug, done properly, with the guard added afterwards and the test still passing.

items.t: Merkle airdrop replay, on camera
items.d: The video treatment of the article in Web3 Topics: one valid proof claimed twice because a leaf was never marked spent.

items.t: Signature replay across forks, demonstrated on two chains
items.d: The video treatment of the article in Web3 Topics — the same signature accepted twice, then chainId binding closing it live.

items.t: Forging signatures with invalid v values
items.d: ecrecover returning an unexpected address, and the check that was missing.

items.t: Selfdestruct, live: force-feeding ETH to break an accounting assumption
items.d: The video treatment of the article in Web3 Topics — force-fed balance breaking an invariant, on camera, in under ten minutes.

items.t: Front-running simulation with vm.prank and vm.txGasPrice
items.d: Building the mempool race inside Foundry so the MEV is reproducible.

items.t: Sandwiching a swap on your own AMM
items.d: Front-run, victim transaction, back-run — with the extracted value printed.

items.t: The inflation attack on an ERC-4626 vault
items.d: First-depositor donation, rounding, and the three defences compared on camera.

items.t: Calldata bomb: DoSing a contract with an oversized payload
items.d: Gas exhaustion as an availability attack rather than a theft.

items.t: From phishing to drain: a key compromise simulation
items.d: The non-code half of security, walked through end to end.

groups.title: Series: EVM under the hood
groups.note: Short, dense, highly linkable. These age well and get embedded in other people's posts.

items.t: Assembly debugging: reading raw calldata
items.d: Decode a real transaction's calldata by hand before letting a tool do it.

items.t: Reading another contract's private variables with vm.load
items.d: Two minutes, one slot, and the end of 'private means hidden'.

items.t: Deploying the same contract at two addresses with create2
items.d: Salt, init code hash, and the address computed before deployment.

items.t: Fallback versus receive, four sends on screen
items.d: The video treatment of the article in Web3 Topics: four cases, with the dispatch decision shown for each.

items.t: Gas profiling: bytes32 versus string in a loop
items.d: The gas report before and after, with the reason in the opcodes.

items.t: Bitwise flags in a single uint256
items.d: Packing eight booleans into one slot and watching the gas drop.

items.t: Forge fuzz test: finding an overflow you did not know existed
items.d: Write the invariant, let the fuzzer find the counterexample, read the shrunk case.

items.t: Why custom errors are cheaper, in the bytecode
items.d: Compile both, diff the output, and show where the string went.

groups.title: Series: Build it from scratch
groups.note: Longer format, 30 to 45 minutes. These convert viewers into subscribers because they are genuinely useful to follow along with.

items.t: A minimal multisig, no OpenZeppelin
items.d: Signature collection, threshold and replay protection, written live.

items.t: A time lock with queue and execute
items.d: Delay, grace period and cancellation, including the window where governance attacks live.

items.t: A minimal ERC-20 in pure Yul
items.d: No Solidity at all — the fastest way to stop guessing about the EVM.

items.t: Building your own multicall
items.d: Aggregation plus the msg.sender subtlety that makes naive versions dangerous.

items.t: A secure relayer with commit and reveal
items.d: The cross-chain pattern, built and then attacked.

items.t: A monitoring dashboard for protocol health
items.d: Tenderly and Dune wired to alerts, built live.

groups.title: Series: Explainers with the maths done properly
groups.note: Whiteboard-style, where the value is deriving rather than asserting.

items.t: Merkle trees and Merkle proofs, derived
items.d: Build the tree by hand, then the proof, then the verification — with the arithmetic visible.

items.t: Account abstraction, explained with the maths
items.d: ERC-4337 flow, the UserOperation lifecycle, and who pays for what.

items.t: The Ethereum Yellow Paper, chapter by chapter
items.d: A long-running series. Nobody has done this well, and the first three episodes would rank for years.

items.t: Mastering Ethereum, chapter by chapter
items.d: The approachable companion series to the Yellow Paper one.

items.t: Uniswap V3 ticks and Q64.96, on a whiteboard
items.d: The fixed-point maths that confuses everyone, derived from scratch.

items.t: The 63/64 gas rule, visualised
items.d: Why a guard that relied on running out of gas stopped working.

items.t: Seven-layer security model for cross-chain
items.d: The framework, then a real bridge mapped onto it.

groups.title: Series: Audit walkthroughs

items.t: Auditing a bridge contract: live walkthrough
items.d: One contract, one hour, thinking out loud including the dead ends.

items.t: Finding five bugs in one hour
items.d: A deliberately seeded codebase, timed, with the method narrated.

items.t: Foundry fork testing: simulating mainnet conditions
items.d: Forking at a block, impersonating a whale, and reproducing a real incident.

items.t: Post-mortem writing workshop: from exploit to report
items.d: Turning a finding into the deliverable a client pays for.

items.t: Web3 attack vectors playlist: reentrancy first
items.d: Start with what the class is, then work through the post-mortems. The playlist is the product.
